A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoTP research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-G are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original mid-training, SFT, RL, ablation, scaling, and reasoning-pattern results in Sections 3-4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and reports additional Chinese-versus-English pattern-similarity results and STEM pattern visualizations in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 revises core-set answer validation from manual screening to independently generated answers from multiple strong reasoning models and majority voting. Manual selection of important traces remains, as do TF-IDF weighting, entropy and pattern distances, weighted DTW, and Hungarian assignment.

E1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds Chinese-versus-English pattern representations as input conditions for similarity evaluation. F.3 extends qualitative analysis to physics, chemistry, biology, and computer science using existing training data. The training corpora and downstream benchmark coverage remain unchanged; no new STEM performance evaluations are reported.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same dataset-based baselines, including OpenR1-Math, AM-Distilled, and LongCoTPool. RL comparator membership and the entropy, n-gram, and importance ablation variants also remain unchanged. The new language analysis does not introduce another data-selection baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix F.2 introduces a protocol using sampled CoTP pattern pairs, manual selection of unrelated pairs, and comparison of mean and binned character-level n-gram similarities across languages. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. The newly stated 12B-token ablation budget is a disclosure, not sufficient evidence that the earlier experiments used a different budget.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2 adds quantitative analysis and error examples supporting Chinese pattern labels; F.3 adds high- versus low-importance pattern visualizations across four STEM domains. The existing component ablations retain their variants but receive a revised full-CoTP reference row. These are focused extensions and revisions to the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 retains 32 repetitions for AIME and HMMT, 10 for BeyondAIME, and one evaluation for MATH500. Ablation uncertainties already appeared in v1 Appendix Table 9; moving them into v3 Table 3 does not introduce a new reporting practice. No new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is stated.

E6.justification: The full-CoTP ablation average changes from 37.53 in v1 Tables 3/9 to 30.68 in v3 Table 3, while the no-entropy average remains 29.93, reducing the reported gap from 7.60 to 0.75 points. This revised reference accompanies the disclosed 12B setting, rather than establishing a same-setting performance decline. New similarity results include 0.035 for Chinese versus 0.541 for English unrelated pairs. Main benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The model-potential definition, geometric first-passage relationship, assignment formulation, and Appendix B proof are substantively unchanged. Separately displaying TF-IDF weighting and regrouping or renumbering equations add no new mathematics. The added low-K motivation is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about reasoning potential, dual-granularity CoTP selection, and improved mathematical reasoning and downstream RL. The headline 9.58-point AIME and 7.81-point RL advantages are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation attributing weaker general performance relative to OpenR1-Math and AM-Distilled to BoostQA within the source mixture, and explicitly frames DeepSeek-R1 as a proxy for the ideal model. It also interprets English similarity errors through shared suffixes and uses STEM visualizations to argue broader applicability. These extend interpretation without adding downstream generalization evidence.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote changes from promising code and data to stating their availability and providing a repository link. Section 3.3 newly specifies the 12B-token ablation blend and its 1:2 reasoning-data-to-KnowEdu ratio. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. External resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tu et al.'s survey on LLM mid-training and replaces the Munkres assignment reference with Mills-Tettey et al.'s dynamic Hungarian algorithm reference. Other prominent citation changes update metadata or consolidate references to the same works. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 reformats the contributions as a numbered list, expands selected motivation and interpretation passages, updates affiliations, and adds Appendix F.2-F.3. Ablation details are consolidated into Section 3.3. Most prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The compact main-text ablation table and fuller appendix table become one full-width main-text Table 3. v3 adds three language-analysis tables and an eight-panel STEM Figure 11. Existing figures retain their content, with some relocation or resizing; subsequent case-study tables and entropy figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the component evidence more transparent through the explicit ablation budget and revised CoTP reference, adds direct evidence for the Chinese-label choice, and supplies code/data access information. The gains are limited: headline experiments remain unchanged, the new pattern-pair analysis omits its sample count, and STEM word clouds provide only qualitative support for broad applicability.
